config.title: What does the key norm destroy at hd=4 — per-token magnitude or direction? Decomposing the k-side cliff on paired inits
config.hypothesis: 2026-08-30 rewrote the thread's cliff story: at hd=4 the KEY norm pays essentially the full qknorm cliff (k-norm-only +0.127 vs qknorm +0.130) while the query norm is nearly free (+0.024) - contradicting 08-02/06, which had localized the cliff to q-side per-token magnitude destruction because an undetached q-magnitude channel closed 98% of it (but was only ever tested on top of FULL qknorm, where q-compensation exists). Tonight decomposes what the key norm destroys at hd=4, on byte-identical paired inits: the learnable gain (norm-without-gain / gain-without-norm), the per-token magnitude VALUE (detached-magnitude-restore: normalize the direction but multiply back the detached per-token k-RMS, making the forward pass equal to gain-only while gradients still flow through the normalized geometry), and the magnitude GRADIENT channel (undetached dynk on top of k-norm-only - the 08-06 machinery finally tested without a free q-side). Predictions registered up front: P1 if the cliff is per-token key-magnitude VALUE destruction, magrestore recovers most of it and gain-only stays at baseline; P2 the gain is not the cliff (nogain ~ knorm_only), per 08-23's frozen-gain result; P3 if 08-02's "key-side restoration hurts" was a full-qknorm artifact, undetached dynk should now HELP on top of k-norm-only.
